source_text: Deinde cum in Testamentis agi ea, quae sunt promissa, conspicimus, praesentis vitae inter ludicra omnino omnia bona malaque numeramus fidem pollicitationis Dei de magnitudine in nos caritatis illius aestimantes. Neque enim confutabit spem nostram aeternorum frustratio commodorum, quandoquidem vadem beatitudinis futurae Dei caritatem tenemus, quae effusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum Sanctum, qui datus est nobis [n253] , id est per dona Sancti Spiritus amorem suum Deus circa genus probavit humanum.
pass_a_gloss: Next when we look at those things which have been promised being acted in the Testaments, we number among the playthings of the present life altogether all goods and evils, estimating the faith of God's promise from the greatness of that love toward us. For a frustration of eternal advantages will not confute our hope, seeing that we hold as a surety of future beatitude the love of God, which has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us, that is through the gifts of the Holy Spirit God has proved his love around the human race.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Then, when we see the promises of the Testaments being fulfilled, we count absolutely all the good and evil things of present life among trifles. We judge the trustworthiness of God’s promise from the greatness of his love toward us. The disappointment of eternal benefits will not refute our hope, because we hold God’s love as a guarantor of future blessedness. It ‘has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us’ (Romans 5:5): that is, through the Holy Spirit’s gifts God has proved his love for the human race.

choices.why: Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.
Julian's name for the doctrine he attacks: evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
